Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

[{"id": "arka-english-main-0-transcribe-medium-0274", "row_sha256": "9e7a6b4200348a93971f97811c26a76b83dd2d91d04db6153001eb8326f64131", "mode": "/transcribe", "language": "en", "context": {}, "identity": false, "mode_instructions": "Remove true hesitation and accidental restarts. Apply explicit corrections to the final stated intent. Preserve meaningful filler-like words and unfinished thoughts. Apply clearly spoken punctuation and list cues. Keep the supplied language.", "input": "um the rain gauge behind the library was reading higher than the one on cedar street after the storm on tuesday and we wanted to check whether the difference came from the wind or from water running off the roof the station has a small screen under the awning and a paper log inside the cabinet so i compared both before the morning volunteers arrived marta was unlocking the gate when i asked if she had noticed the funnel rocking overnight she said uh-huh and pointed to a loose bracket near the fence well that explained why the gauge might have caught extra drops but it did not explain the full difference i wrote down the time and took a photo of the screen before we adjusted anything the reading was 18 millimeters at the library and 12 on cedar street the sidewalk was still wet and leaves had collected around the drain like a shallow ring we cleared the leaves away and checked that the funnel was level actually the bracket had shifted only a little so we tightened it and left the gauge in place i asked the afternoon volunteer to compare the next reading with the cedar street log and note whether the wind picked up again", "output": "The rain gauge behind the library was reading higher than the one on Cedar Street after the storm on Tuesday, and we wanted to check whether the difference came from the wind or from water running off the roof. The station has a small screen under the awning and a paper log inside the cabinet, so I compared both before the morning volunteers arrived. Marta was unlocking the gate when I asked if she had noticed the funnel rocking overnight. She said, “Uh-huh,” and pointed to a loose bracket near the fence. Well, that explained why the gauge might have caught extra drops, but it did not explain the full difference. I wrote down the time and took a photo of the screen before we adjusted anything. The reading was 18 millimeters at the library and 12 on Cedar Street. The sidewalk was still wet, and leaves had collected around the drain like a shallow ring. We cleared the leaves away and checked that the funnel was level. Actually, the bracket had shifted only a little, so we tightened it and left the gauge in place. I asked the afternoon volunteer to compare the next reading with the Cedar Street log and note whether the wind picked up again."}]
